tweets.text:
America’s next 250 years can look like that. 🎯

NASA already sent the machine into the dark first.

Two American rovers are still driving Mars in 2026. Curiosity has been climbing Mount Sharp since 2012 — 14 years, 42 drill holes, a full kilometer of elevation this August. Perseverance landed in 2021 and ran a marathon (26.2 miles) in five years and four months. Opportunity needed more than eleven years for the same distance. About 90% of Perseverance’s driving is autonomous. It cached 33 of 43 sample tubes. MOXIE pulled the first oxygen ever made from another planet’s air — 122 grams of proof you can live off the land. Ingenuity flew 72 times before it retired: first powered aircraft on another world.

No siren. No speech. Just a robot crawling toward a trapped guy.

Mine collapse. Dust. Black tunnel. One headlight. The machine is on its hands and knees. It finds the miner and reaches out. He reaches back toward the only light left down there.

That’s the thesis. If the roof might still fall, you don’t send your friend first. You send AI. NASA has been running that play on another planet for 29 years.

Same move in surgery. NASA-backed robots already cut on Earth and demonstrated from the ISS. On a Mars transit the radio lag can hit 45 minutes. NASA’s medical models list ~20–27 conditions that may need a knife. Nobody is flying a specialist in tomorrow. The clinic on site has to be elite the first time.

If you’re 22, this is not a documentary about old people. This is the stack you get to live inside.

xAI’s job is the mind: AI that actually tries to understand the universe, then puts that understanding where a bad call costs a life. Grok is the layer that never sleeps — history, vitals, scans, physics — so the best call isn’t locked behind whoever survived admissions. Tesla Optimus is the body that can crawl the unstable tunnel and hold the instruments. SpaceX is the ride. NASA already paved the map: Artemis II flew crew around the Moon in April 2026 for America 250. First landing is targeted for Artemis IV in 2028. Then a lunar outpost. Then Mars.

Earth still has backup. Mars doesn’t.

No extra hospital two cities over. If a habitat cracks or a settler codes, robots print the base, check the lava tube, keep oxygen honest, operate when a human body is the wrong tool. xAI-class models run the plan. Optimus does the work. Humans stay responsible.

A million robots on Mars is not “humans are finished.” It’s how you stop betting every consciousness you’ve got on one wet planet.

Keep the rules adult:
you consent to the machine
a human still owns the call
the robot in Ohio or in a Mars dome is as good as the one in a flagship hospital
somebody with a pulse is still in the room
That’s the optimistic version of AI. Not a god. Not a villain. The thing that walks into the dark first — the same way NASA’s machines have been walking Mars since Sojourner.
America’s next 250 years can look like that. Robot crawls first. Robot takes the scalpel. You still stand there. People live. Mars gets built. The species doesn’t die finding out the tunnel wasn’t stable.
